claims.text: A full-text search of the released AARO Historical Record Report Volume I returns no occurrence of 'Yankee Blue'. The term is likewise absent from the FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 consolidated annual reports.
The claim that AARO acknowledged Yankee Blue in Volume I is widely repeated in reporting and was asserted on this board until 12 Aug 2026. It does not survive a full-text check of the document.

NEGATIVE PRIMARY FINDING: a full-text search of the released AARO Historical Record Report Volume I (63 pp., DOPSR-cleared 6 Mar 2024) returns zero hits for 'Yankee', 'Kirtland', 'AFOSI', 'Office of Special Investigations', 'initiation' and 'hazing'. Yankee Blue is NOT documented in HRR Volume I. Any citation of Volume I as the source for the Yankee Blue / Kirtland-AFOSI account is incorrect.

The only named sensitive programs disclosed in HRR Volume I's Section VI ('Investigation into Named USG Sensitive Programs', pp. 33-36) are KONA BLUE, the Virtual Institute for Satellite Integration Training, and an unnamed IC Controlled Access Program 'unnecessarily expanded in 2021 to include a UAP reverse-engineering mission'. Yankee Blue is not among them.

Yankee Blue therefore has no Tier 1 anchor in the AARO documentary record as of 12 Aug 2026. The public account rests on June 2025 press reporting and on statements attributed to AARO officials describing an Air Force hazing/indoctrination practice at Kirtland AFB in which personnel were falsely read into a non-existent UAP program; the underlying memo has not been released. Reasoning: direct full-text verification against the only AARO report that could plausibly have contained it, plus the absence of any Yankee Blue reference in the FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 annual reports (also searched, zero hits).

OSD's final response in FOIA case 25-F-3514 (September 2025) stated that after 'thorough searches of the electronic records and files of CMD, no records of the kind you described could be identified' regarding the alleged spring 2023 cessation memo.
In case 2025-06002-F, AFOSI stated it found 'no records' of investigative reports, summaries or closure memos tied to 'Yankee Blue.'

desc: YANKEE BLUE is the allegation that the US Air Force ran a fake UFO reverse-engineering programme on its own personnel — briefing officers in classified units into believing they had been read on to a recovery effort, using fabricated material, as a counterintelligence or hazing exercise. If documented it would be the strongest single item in the coverup strand, because it is the government generating false UAP belief inside its own ranks. It is not documented. A full-text search of the released AARO Historical Record Report Volume I (63 pp., March 2024) finds no occurrence of the term, and it appears in none of the FY2023, FY2024 or FY2025 consolidated annual reports — which corrects a widely repeated claim, including one this board previously made, that AARO conceded the programme in Volume I. Two FOIA cases have returned negative: OSD case 25-F-3514 (September 2025) reported no responsive records after searches of the electronic and paper holdings, and AFOSI case 2025-06002-F reported no investigative reports, summaries or closure memoranda. On 1 October 2025 Pentagon spokesperson Susan Gough stated she could not confirm the alleged memorandum. The Department reportedly reopened the search in December 2025 with no published result. The programme is retained on the board at Tier B with the allegation graded Tier 3 and the negative FOIA findings graded Tier 1. A negative primary finding is itself a documented fact and belongs on a board about concealment — but it is a finding about the absence of a record, not a record.

claims.source: Joel Schectman and Aruna Viswanatha, "The Pentagon Disinformation That Fueled America's UFO Mythology," The Wall Street Journal, 6 June 2025, https://www.wsj.com/politics/national-security/ufo-us-disinformation-45376f7e
claims.text: The Wall Street Journal reported on 6 June 2025 that AARO, under its first director Sean Kirkpatrick, found that personnel in classified Air Force units had for decades been shown flying-saucer imagery and told they were being read on to a reverse-engineering programme called YANKEE BLUE that did not exist.

The Wall Street Journal reported that a directive from the office of the Secretary of Defense was circulated across the services in spring 2023 ordering the practice to stop immediately. The article did not publish the memorandum, identify its date or describe its sourcing, and no such document has surfaced publicly.

A FOIA request filed with the Office of the Secretary of Defense on 17 June 2025 sought any spring 2023 directive halting YANKEE BLUE-related practices; OSD searched solely within its Correspondence Management Division and reported no responsive records in September 2025.

Pentagon spokesperson Susan Gough stated on 1 October 2025: "Regarding the alleged memo: I cannot confirm the existence of any department-level memo as described in the article. You may want to ask the Air Force or other military services whether they put out such a memo to their personnel." In the original email the word "alleged" was underlined for emphasis.

On 12 December 2025 the Acting Chief of the OSD FOIA Division granted the administrative appeal and wrote: "After carefully considering your appeal, and as a result of discussions between FOID personnel and this office, I am remanding your request to FOID for a search for responsive records."

The appeal, filed 17 September 2025, argued that confining the search to the Correspondence Management Division was not "reasonably calculated to uncover all relevant documents" under Oglesby v. U.S. Dep't of Army, 920 F.2d 57 (D.C. Cir. 1990), and that agencies must pursue logical leads under Campbell v. DOJ, 164 F.3d 20 (D.C. Cir. 1998).
The Air Force did not respond to a request for comment on the alleged directive, and as of 15 December 2025 the FOIA case seeking information on the alleged YANKEE BLUE ritual remained open.

dossier.denialPosture: The Department has not denied the practice and has not confirmed the memorandum. On 1 October 2025 spokesperson Susan Gough stated she could not confirm the existence of any department-level memo as described, underlining the word "alleged," and referred the question to the Air Force and the services; the Air Force did not respond. In September 2025 OSD returned a categorical no-records FOIA determination, which its own appellate authority set aside on 12 December 2025 as resting on an inadequate search.
dossier.narrative:
This entity is retained on the board with the allegation graded low and the negative findings graded high, and the distinction should be kept in front of the reader at all times. A negative primary finding is a documented fact. It is not a record of the thing.

The allegation entered the public record on 6 June 2025, when Joel Schectman and Aruna Viswanatha of The Wall Street Journal published "The Pentagon Disinformation That Fueled America's UFO Mythology." The reporting described a decades-long pattern in which the Air Force encouraged UFO belief to screen classified aviation programmes, and within that pattern a specific practice: personnel in certain classified units were briefed that they were being admitted to a programme called YANKEE BLUE concerned with reverse-engineering recovered non-human craft, shown photographs of saucers, bound by non-disclosure agreements, and in some accounts warned of extreme consequences for disclosure. The practice was said to have run from roughly the Cold War until 2023, when the office of the Secretary of Defense circulated a directive across the services ordering it to stop immediately. The finding was attributed to AARO's internal historical review under Sean Kirkpatrick.

Everything downstream of that article is either restatement or an attempt to find the paper. Popular Mechanics, VICE and the New York Post ran versions in June 2025; none produced independent documentation. The article itself, as researcher John Greenewald has noted, did not publish the memorandum, did not identify its date and did not describe its sourcing.

The documentary trail that does exist is a FOIA trail, and it is unusually clean because it has been published in full. On 17 June 2025 Greenewald's Black Vault filed a request with the Office of the Secretary of Defense for any directive issued in spring 2023 ordering a halt to YANKEE BLUE-related practices or to other activities involving fabricated claims of reverse-engineering non-human technology. OSD searched solely within its Correspondence Management Division and reported no responsive records. On 17 September 2025 an administrative appeal was filed arguing that a search confined to one office was not "reasonably calculated to uncover all relevant documents" under Oglesby v. U.S. Dep't of Army, 920 F.2d 57 (D.C. Cir. 1990), that a Secretary-level directive could reasonably reside in policy directorates or the OSD Executive Secretariat, and that agencies must pursue logical leads under Campbell v. DOJ, 164 F.3d 20 (D.C. Cir. 1998). The appeal also made the records-management point directly: any such 2023 memorandum would be subject to mandatory federal retention, so its absence is itself a finding.

On 1 October 2025, asked again about the WSJ claim, Pentagon spokesperson Susan Gough replied: "Regarding the alleged memo: I cannot confirm the existence of any department-level memo as described in the article. You may want to ask the Air Force or other military services whether they put out such a memo to their personnel." In the original email the word "alleged" was underlined. This is a carefully constructed sentence. It does not deny that the practice occurred. It denies confirmation of a department-level memorandum and redirects to the services. The Air Force did not respond to a request for comment.

On 12 December 2025 the Acting Chief of the OSD FOIA Division ruled on the appeal: "After carefully considering your appeal, and as a result of discussions between FOID personnel and this office, I am remanding your request to FOID for a search for responsive records." The appellate decision, released as case 25-A-3514-A1, does not establish that the memorandum exists. It establishes that the Department's own appellate authority found the Department's prior categorical no-records answer to rest on an inadequate search, and ordered it done again. As of the last published status the case remains open.

There is a second correction this board has already had to make about itself, and it belongs in the dossier. It has been widely repeated - including previously on this board - that AARO acknowledged YANKEE BLUE in its Report on the Historical Record of U.S. Government Involvement with UAP, Volume I, published 8 March 2024. It did not. A full-text check of the released 63-page volume returns no occurrence of the term, and it appears in none of the FY2023, FY2024 or FY2025 consolidated annual reports. The board logged that correction on 12 August 2026. The only official gesture toward the subject is the Department's statement, made in the context of the June 2025 reporting, that it "is committed to releasing a second volume of its Historical Record Report, to include AARO's findings on reports of potential pranks and inauthentic materials," then expected in late 2025. No such volume was located in the sources available for this dossier, which means the sole official channel through which the finding was to be documented had not delivered as of the research cutoff.

So the honest state of the record is this. A major newspaper reported a specific, named, dated practice sourced to a Pentagon office's internal review. The Pentagon has neither confirmed nor denied the practice, has said it cannot confirm the memorandum, has failed one FOIA search on appeal, has been ordered to search again, has promised a report volume that would address it, and has not published that volume. Every one of those is an artifact of an institution's conduct and every one of them is dated and attributable. None of them is the programme. YANKEE BLUE stays on this board as a node about the Department's disclosure behaviour, and it should not be cited by anyone as established fact about what was done to Air Force personnel until a document with a signature block exists.
openQuestions: Does the spring 2023 Secretary of Defense directive exist? The remanded OSD search ordered on 12 December 2025 has not published a result.
If no such directive exists, what did the Wall Street Journal's sources describe, and will the newspaper address the discrepancy?
Did any service - Air Force, Space Force or otherwise - issue its own stop order, as Gough's referral implies might be the case?
Has AARO Historical Record Report Volume II been published, and does it contain the pranks and inauthentic-materials findings the Department promised?

Are there AFOSI investigative files, closure memoranda or IG referrals on the practice? The case number carried in this project's correction record has not been verified against a released response letter.
Has any named individual gone on the record as having been indoctrinated into YANKEE BLUE? As of this dossier, no such person has been publicly identified.
Has any Senate Armed Services or House Oversight correspondence named the programme? No such correspondence was located.
dossier.whatItIs: YANKEE BLUE is an alleged United States Air Force practice in which personnel entering certain classified units were shown photographs of flying saucers and told they were being read on to a programme to reverse-engineer non-human craft, when no such programme existed. It was reported in June 2025 by The Wall Street Journal as a finding of the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office under its first director, Sean Kirkpatrick, and was said to have been halted by a spring 2023 directive from the office of the Secretary of Defense. No primary document establishing the programme, the practice or the directive has been released.
dossier.whyImplicated: If documented, YANKEE BLUE would be the single strongest item in the concealment strand of this board, because it is the government manufacturing belief in a recovery and reverse-engineering programme inside its own ranks - which means that some fraction of insider testimony about that programme could be the product of a deliberate indoctrination rather than of access. It cuts both ways and it cuts hard, which is exactly why the tiering here has to be strict. What is documented is not the programme. What is documented is the Department's behaviour when asked for the paper: an Office of the Secretary of Defense FOIA search confined to a single correspondence office returning no records in September 2025, a Pentagon spokesperson on 1 October 2025 stating she could not confirm the memorandum with the word "alleged" underlined for emphasis, and an OSD appellate authority on 12 December 2025 overturning that search as inadequate and remanding for a new one. A department that cannot locate a Secretary-level directive from 2023 has either a records problem or a candour problem, and either is on the map.

entityInfo.desc: The board's position on YANKEE BLUE is deliberately unresolved, and the reason is instructive. If the Wall Street Journal's June 2025 account is accurate, the Air Force ran, for something on the order of two decades, an institutionalised deception in which personnel were falsely read into a fictitious reverse-engineering programme - which would mean that a substantial share of the insider testimony in this field originates in a disinformation operation, and would simultaneously prove that the US Air Force runs disinformation operations about UFOs on its own people at scale. Either conclusion is damaging to the government. But the paper trail is missing. The Office of the Secretary of Defense searched its Correspondence Management Division and reported no records of the alleged spring 2023 cessation memo (case 25-F-3514, September 2025). It could not locate briefing materials prepared for DNI Avril Haines on the subject (case 25-F-3515, under appeal). AFOSI reported no records of any investigation (case 2025-06002-F). On 1 October 2025 the Pentagon's spokesperson said she could not confirm the memo existed and suggested asking the services. On 15 December 2025 an appellate decision found the CMD-only search inadequate under Oglesby v. U.S. Dep't of Army, 920 F.2d 57 (D.C. Cir. 1990) and remanded. So there are exactly three possibilities and the board holds all three open: the memo exists and the department cannot find its own Secretary-level directives; the memo does not exist and a major newspaper's central sourced claim about Pentagon conduct is unsupported; or the memo exists in a channel FOIA does not reach. The first and third are the concealment thesis. The second is a caution against accepting any account, including a debunking account, without the paper.

timeline.label: WSJ reports the 'Yankee Blue' disinformation practice
timeline.text: The Wall Street Journal reports that the Air Force falsely convinced personnel they were on a reverse-engineering programme for decades, and that OSD ordered the practice halted in spring 2023.

timeline.label: Yankee Blue exposed
timeline.text: The Wall Street Journal reports that the Air Force ran a fictitious alien-technology programme on its own personnel for decades - NDAs, saucer photographs, threats - halted by an OSD memorandum in spring 2023. DNI Haines was briefed that hundreds and hundreds were affected. DoD says the findings will appear in Volume II.

timeline.label: Pentagon: no records of the Yankee Blue memo
timeline.text: OSD responds in FOIA case 25-F-3514 that no records of the alleged cessation memo could be identified; AFOSI reports no records of any related investigation.

timeline.label: Pentagon spokesperson cannot confirm the memo
timeline.text: Susan Gough: 'Regarding the alleged memo: I cannot confirm the existence of any department-level memo as described in the article.'

timeline.label: FOIA appeal granted; search remanded
